test_title: PYST 45 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 29 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
"The Japanese education system also strongly focuses on moral training, teamwork, and responsibility,"

why is the verb** "focuses"** used instead of **"focus"**?

options.text: Because the sentence is in passive voice

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2 (Because "system" is a singular subject)**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• ***Option 1: Because "training" is the object***

 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The verb form is determined by the subject, not the object. “Training” is the object of the verb “focuses.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Because "system" is a singular subject***
 
 
• This is **correct**. The subject of the sentence is “The Japanese education system,” which is singular. Therefore, the verb must agree in the singular form: “focuses.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Because "education" is uncountable***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While “education” is uncountable, the subject is “system,” not “education.” The verb agreement depends on “system.”
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Because the sentence is in passive voice***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The sentence is in active voice (“system focuses”), not passive. Passive would be “is focused on.”
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**: *Because "system" is a singular subject.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Subject-verb agreement rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb form (with -s or -es in present tense).
 
• Example: “The committee **decides** the rules.” / “The system **works** efficiently.”
 
• If the subject were plural (“systems”), the verb would be “focus.”
